include.description: Reads more config files first, by path or pattern. What this file says wins.

default-profile.description: New tabs open with the profile that has this id.

profile-order.description: The menus list profiles in this order, by id.

keys.description: Binds a key chord or sequence, like ctrl+shift+t or ctrl+a > c, to the action it runs. A key bound to none goes to the program instead.
keys.markdownDescription: Binds a key chord or sequence, like `ctrl+shift+t` or `ctrl+a > c`, to the action it runs. A key bound to `none` goes to the program instead.

family.title: Font
family.description: Any monospace font. Nerd Fonts also show prompt icons.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: How heavy normal text is. A font without that weight shows its nearest one.

ligatures.title: Ligatures
ligatures.description: Fonts that have them (Cascadia Code, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code) join =>, !=, ->, and the like into one shape. Each character keeps its own cell, and the character under the cursor isn't joined.
ligatures.markdownDescription: Fonts that have them (Cascadia Code, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code) join `=>`, `!=`, `->`, and the like into one shape. Each character keeps its own cell, and the character under the cursor isn't joined.

fallback.title: Fallback fonts
fallback.description: Zinc tries these fonts in order for characters your font lacks, before Windows picks one. Separate them with commas.

adjust-cell-height.title: Line height
adjust-cell-height.description: Adds room between lines, as a percentage (20%) or in pixels (2). A negative value gives less room. Text stays centered.

builtin-glyphs.title: Built-in glyphs
builtin-glyphs.description: Zinc draws box lines, blocks, and Powerline shapes itself, so they join up in any font.

adjust-box-thickness.title: Line thickness
adjust-box-thickness.description: Makes built-in lines thicker or thinner, in pixels (1, -1) or as a percentage (20%).

theme.title: Color scheme
theme.description: About 650 schemes are included. Add your own to the themes folder next to config.toml.

palette-generate.title: Match 256 colors to the scheme
palette-generate.description: Programs that use the extended 256 colors (vim and htop themes) get shades made from the scheme's 16 colors instead of the standard ones.

palette-harmonious.title: Shades from background to text in light schemes
palette-harmonious.description: When off, shades run from dark to light, which is what programs expect.

cursor-text.title: Cursor text
cursor-text.description: Colors the character under a block cursor. If the scheme doesn't set one either, it's the background color.

selection-background.title: Selection
selection-background.description: Colors the background of selected text. If the scheme doesn't set one either, selection inverts the colors.

selection-foreground.title: Selected text
selection-foreground.description: If the scheme doesn't set one either, the text keeps its color, or inverts with the selection when "Selection" has no color either.

pane-header.title: Pane headers
pane-header.description: Colors the row behind pane titles and tabs. On cards, the border is a step stronger.

minimum-contrast.title: Minimum contrast
minimum-contrast.description: Text that reads poorly against its background turns black or white. 1 turns it off, 4.5 is the usual accessibility level, and 21 makes all text black or white.

bold-is-bright.title: Bold in bright colors
bold-is-bright.description: Bold text in the first eight colors shows their bright versions, as older terminals did.

bold.title: Bold text color
bold.description: Colors bold text that's in the default text color.

faint-opacity.title: Faint text
faint-opacity.description: How bright dim text is. At 1, dim text is as bright as other text.

find-highlight.title: Find highlight
find-highlight.description: Colors the background of each match of Find.

find-highlight-current.title: Current match
find-highlight-current.description: Colors the background of the match Find is on.

cursor-opacity.title: Cursor opacity
cursor-opacity.description: At 1, the cursor is solid. Lower values let the character under a block cursor show in its own color.

background-opacity.title: Terminal background opacity
background-opacity.description: At 1, the background is solid. Lower values let the window background show behind the text. Colored cells stay solid.

palette.description: Palette colors by number (palette.1 = "#AC4242") are set in config.toml.

cursor-style.title: Cursor shape
cursor-style.description: A program can pick its own shape, as vim's insert mode often does.

cursor-blink.title: Blinking cursor
cursor-blink.description: A program can turn blinking on or off for itself.

cursor-style-at-prompt.title: Cursor at the prompt
cursor-style-at-prompt.description: The cursor takes this shape while the shell waits for a command. A program's own cursor still wins. Needs shell integration.

padding-x.title: Padding left and right
padding-x.description: Adds space between the window's edge and the text.

padding-y.title: Padding top and bottom
padding-y.description: Adds space between the window's edge and the text.

padding-balance.title: Even padding
padding-balance.description: Splits the leftover space between both sides. When off, all of it goes to the right and bottom.

shell-integration.title: Shell integration
shell-integration.description: Marks prompts and commands in PowerShell, bash, and zsh (WSL too), so you can jump between prompts, copy a command's output, and see which commands failed.

command-marks.title: Command marks
command-marks.description: Shows a bar beside the output of these commands.

reload-environment.title: Pick up environment changes
reload-environment.description: New tabs read PATH and other variables from Windows as they start, so an installer's changes work without restarting Zinc.

program-titles.title: Program titles
program-titles.description: Shells and programs set the tab's title (often the folder or the running command). When off, tabs show the profile's name.

shell-titles.title: Folder and command as the title
shell-titles.description: Shows the folder at the prompt, and the running command otherwise. A program's own title still wins. Needs shell integration.

scrollback-lines.title: Scrollback lines
scrollback-lines.description: How far back you can scroll.

word-boundaries.title: Word boundaries
word-boundaries.description: These characters end a word when you double-click. Space and tab always do. When this is empty, Zinc uses the characters shown.

click-to-move.title: Click to move the cursor
click-to-move.description: At a shell prompt, clicking in the command you're typing moves the cursor there. Needs shell integration.

right-click.title: Right-click
right-click.description: Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the menu anywhere.

link-click.title: Open links with
link-click.description: Web links and files in the terminal open with this.

middle-click-paste.title: Middle-click pastes
middle-click-paste.description: Pastes the clipboard unless the program uses the mouse.

copy-on-select.title: Copy on select
copy-on-select.description: Copies text as soon as you select it. The selection stays.

copy-formatting.title: Copy with formatting
copy-formatting.description: Copies colors and styles too, for documents and email. Apps that take plain text still get plain text.

paste-warning.title: Paste warning
paste-warning.description: Asks before pasting text with more than one line.

large-paste-warning.title: Large pastes
large-paste-warning.description: Asks before pasting more than 5 KB.

clipboard-write.title: Programs may copy
clipboard-write.description: Copying with OSC 52, as tmux, Neovim, and remote shells do.

clipboard-read.title: Programs reading the clipboard
clipboard-read.description: Anything running, including a remote host, could read the clipboard.

bell.title: Bell
bell.description: Says what happens when a program rings the bell, for example at a failed tab completion.

screen-flash-bell.title: Visual bell
screen-flash-bell.description: Programs that flash the screen instead of beeping (Git Bash does) ring Zinc's bell, as set in "Bell".

input-method.title: Input methods
input-method.description: Type Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and more with Windows' input methods (IME). Turn it off if keys behave oddly.

appearance.title: Light or dark
appearance.description: Sets the look of Zinc's windows, menus, and dialogs. The terminal keeps its color scheme. Restart Zinc to apply.

accent.title: Accent color
accent.description: Colors selections, focus lines, switches, and buttons. Restart Zinc to apply.

backdrop.title: Window background
backdrop.description: What's behind everything in the window: tabs, sidebar, and terminal.

backdrop-tint.title: Window tint
backdrop-tint.description: How much color an acrylic or clear background carries. Lower is more see-through.

backdrop-color.title: Window tint color
backdrop-color.description: The color an acrylic or clear background is tinted with.

workspace-tabs.title: Workspaces
workspace-tabs.description: Shows workspaces as tabs along the top, or as a list in a sidebar. Applies to windows opened from now on.

sidebar.title: Sidebar
sidebar.description: Applies only when "Workspaces" is "In a sidebar".

title-bar.title: Title bar
title-bar.description: Applies only when "Workspaces" is "In a sidebar".

new-workspace-page.title: Start page for new workspaces
new-workspace-page.description: Lets you choose a profile, a folder, and a name when you open a workspace. Enter starts the default profile.

workspace-colors.title: Colors for new workspaces
workspace-colors.description: New workspaces you don't color yourself take their colors from this.

start-in.title: New tabs and splits start
start-in.description: New tabs in a workspace with its own folder start there. Without "Tabs inside panes", this is for splits only, because a new tab is a new workspace.

pane-tabs.title: Tabs inside panes
pane-tabs.description: Each pane can hold several tabs.

pane-tabs-as.title: Show pane tabs as
pane-tabs-as.description: Applies only while "Tabs inside panes" is on.

pane-headers.title: Pane headers
pane-headers.description: The row above a pane shows its tabs, or its title when it has one tab.

pane-header-buttons.title: Header buttons
pane-header-buttons.description: Shows split, maximize, and other buttons on the right of a pane's header, with a program's progress beside them.

pane-gap.title: Gap between panes
pane-gap.description: Above 0, panes are rounded cards with space between them. At 0 they meet at a thin divider.

pane-gap-edges.title: Gap at the workspace edges
pane-gap-edges.description: Puts the same gap around the outside, split or not, so splitting never moves a pane's outer edges. Applies only when "Gap between panes" is above 0.

pane-focus.title: Show focus with
pane-focus.description: How the focused pane stands out from the others.

pane-animations.title: Pane animations
pane-animations.description: Panes slide into place when you split, close, maximize, or move them. They don't while "Animation effects" is off in Windows Settings.

pane-resize-step.title: Resize step
pane-resize-step.description: How far a resize key moves the divider, as a share of the panes it splits.

unfocused-pane-opacity.title: Unfocused panes
unfocused-pane-opacity.description: How bright unfocused panes stay. At 1, they aren't dimmed.

unfocused-pane-fill.title: Dimming color
unfocused-pane-fill.description: Unfocused panes fade toward this color.

divider-color.title: Divider color
divider-color.description: Colors the line between split panes when "Gap between panes" is 0.

save-state.title: Reopen windows
save-state.description: Windows, workspaces, splits, and tabs come back in their folders.

launch-at-login.title: When you sign in to Windows

explorer-menu.title: Open in Zinc from File Explorer
explorer-menu.description: Adds "Open in Zinc" to the right-click menu of folders and drives. On Windows 11 it's under "Show more options".

confirm-close.title: Ask before closing
confirm-close.description: Asks when a tab, pane, workspace, or window you close still runs a command or holds two or more tabs. Zinc knows a command is running through shell integration.

confirm-quit.title: Ask before quitting with a running command
confirm-quit.description: Asks when you quit Zinc, or restart it for an update, while a command still runs.

focus-follows-mouse.title: Focus follows mouse
focus-follows-mouse.description: Moving the pointer into a pane focuses it.

low-latency-drawing.title: Low-latency drawing
low-latency-drawing.description: What you type shows up about one screen refresh sooner. Turn it off if a terminal draws wrong or stops drawing, and open an issue. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

free-hidden-memory.title: Free memory of hidden tabs
free-hidden-memory.description: Background tabs, minimized windows, and the dismissed quick terminal give back their graphics memory and rebuild it when you return. Turn it off if switching tabs flashes. Applies only while "Low-latency drawing" is on.

free-hidden-after.title: Free memory after
free-hidden-after.description: This is in seconds unless you add a unit, like 45s or 2m.
free-hidden-after.markdownDescription: This is in seconds unless you add a unit, like `45s` or `2m`.

software-rendering.title: Software rendering
software-rendering.description: Draws with the processor instead of the graphics card, which is slower. Use it for broken graphics drivers, some virtual machines, and remote desktop glitches. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

tab-groups.description: An old name for pane-tabs. It still works.

pane-tab-strip.description: An old name for pane-headers. It still works.

group-tab-strip.description: An old name for pane-headers. It still works.

unfocused-split-opacity.description: An old name for unfocused-pane-opacity. It still works.

unfocused-split-fill.description: An old name for unfocused-pane-fill. It still works.

files.title: Custom shaders
files.description: Effects drawn over the terminal, such as CRT screens, glow, and cursor trails. They're GLSL files written for Ghostty or Shadertoy, and they run in order.

animation.title: Animation
animation.description: Says when animated shaders move. The others redraw only when the terminal changes.

folders.description: Zinc offers the shaders in these folders to choose from. Add and remove folders on the shaders page, in the library's … menu.

remote-control.title: Remote control
remote-control.description: Lets zn, Zinc's command-line tool, open, arrange, and close tabs, type into them, and read them. Any program running as you could use zn.

path.title: Use zn in other terminals
path.description: Adds zn to your PATH, so other terminals find zn too. Zinc's own terminals always do. Shells started from now on see the change.

command-finished.title: Long command finishes
command-finished.description: Says what happens when a long command finishes in a pane you weren't looking at.

command-finished-after.title: Counts as long after
command-finished-after.description: This is in seconds unless you add a unit, like 45s or 2m.
command-finished-after.markdownDescription: This is in seconds unless you add a unit, like `45s` or `2m`.

command-finished-sound.title: Sound
command-finished-sound.description: Plays when a long command finishes out of view. A Windows notification has its own sound.

programs.title: Program notifications
programs.description: Says what happens when a program asks for a notification with OSC 9 or 777, for example when a build script finishes.

finished-color.title: Finished
finished-color.description: A command finished, or a program sent a notification.

failed-color.title: Failed
failed-color.description: A command failed, or a program exited with an error.

hotkey.title: Hotkey
hotkey.description: Shows and hides the quick terminal from anywhere, for example win+grave or ctrl+alt+t.
hotkey.markdownDescription: Shows and hides the quick terminal from anywhere, for example `win+grave` or `ctrl+alt+t`.

size.title: Size
size.description: Sets the quick terminal's size along its edge, as a percentage or in pixels (50%, 600px). When empty, the size is 50%, or 70% by 60% at "Center".
size.markdownDescription: Sets the quick terminal's size along its edge, as a percentage or in pixels (`50%`, `600px`). When empty, the size is 50%, or 70% by 60% at "Center".

animation-duration.title: Animation
animation-duration.description: How long the quick terminal takes to fade in and out. At 0 it appears at once.

check.title: Check for updates automatically
check.description: Zinc checks once a day. New versions download in the background, and you choose when to restart. Only a copy installed with Zinc's installer updates itself.

logging.title: Debug log
logging.description: Keeps a record of what Zinc does, to send with a bug report. Turn it on, make the problem happen, then copy the log.

environment.description: Sets environment variables for the programs Zinc starts. An empty value removes that variable.

name.title: Name
name.description: Menus and tabs show this name.

command.title: Command
command.description: The profile's tabs run this shell or other program.

working-directory.title: Starting folder
working-directory.description: The profile's tabs start in this folder. Write ~ for your home folder, or a path, which can use %VARIABLES%.
working-directory.markdownDescription: The profile's tabs start in this folder. Write `~` for your home folder, or a path, which can use `%VARIABLES%`.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: The profile's tabs show this image file. Without one, they show the program's own icon.

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description: Keeps the profile out of the menus. Its tabs still reopen.

profile.description: A profile, which is a shell or program with settings of its own.
